es.summary: Edema súbito de la piel profunda y de mucosas, frecuentemente en cara, labios, lengua y vías respiratorias, a menudo asociado a urticaria.
key_points: Edema profundo de piel y mucosas que puede comprometer la vía aérea
Desencadenantes comunes: AINES, inhibidores de ECA, alimentos, infecciones
Emergencia si hay dificultad respiratoria o compromiso de la vía aérea
Tratamiento: antihistamínicos, corticoides y epinefrina si hay compromiso
Monitoreo de signos vitales y saturación de oxígeno es esencial

pathophysiology: Liberación de histamina y bradiquinina por reacción alérgica
Aumento de la permeabilidad capilar en dermis profunda y submucosa
Extravasación de líquido al tejido intersticial produciendo edema
risk_factors: Uso de AINES o inhibidores de la ECA (ej. lisinopril)
signs_symptoms: Edema no pruriginoso de labios, párpados, lengua o cara
Sensación de ardor o presión en zona afectada
Silbidos, cianosis si hay obstrucción de vía aérea
diagnostics: Historia clínica y examen físico centrado en la vía aérea
Evaluación de saturación de O₂ y frecuencia respiratoria
Pruebas de alergia (IgE) si se sospecha desencadenante específico
Niveles de C1‑esterasa si se considera angioedema hereditario
treatment: Antihistamínicos H1 de segunda generación (cetirizina) o de primera (difenhidramina)
Epinefrina IM 0.3 mg si hay compromiso respiratorio
Oxígeno suplementario y soporte de vía aérea si es necesario
complications: Obstrucción de vía aérea y asfixia
Edema persistente >72 h con posible daño cutáneo
nursing_care: Evaluar y documentar tamaño del edema cada 15 min inicialmente
Monitorear saturación de O₂ y frecuencia respiratoria
Mantener posición semi‑Fowler para facilitar respiración
Administrar medicamentos según orden y observar respuesta
Preparar equipo de reanimación y epinefrina en caso de deterioro
patient_teaching: Llevar autoinyector de epinefrina si lo prescribe el médico
Buscar atención inmediata si aparece edema facial o dificultad para respirar
Tomar antihistamínicos según indicación y no interrumpir sin consultar
Informar a todos los profesionales de salud sobre su alergia

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
related_to: extravasación de líquido al tejido edematizado
uso de diuréticos o inhibidores de ECA
pérdida de líquidos por secreciones aumentadas
outcomes: Hidratación: nivel adecuado (peso estable, piel turgor normal)
Equilibrio de líquidos: ingesta ≥1500 mL/día mantenida

interventions.action: Monitorear ingesta y eliminación de líquidos cada turno
Evaluar turgor cutáneo y mucosas frecuentemente
Fomentar consumo de líquidos claros si no hay contraindicación
Registrar cambios en el tamaño del edema
interventions.rationale: Observar tendencia de pérdida o acumulación de líquido

interventions.action: Notificar al médico si hay signos de hipotensión o taquicardia
Administrar solución salina según orden si se indica reposición

related_to: sedación por antihistamínicos de primera generación
outcomes: Seguridad de la vía aérea: sin signos de aspiración durante la hospitalización
Función respiratoria: saturación de O₂ ≥95 % en reposo

interventions.action: Mantener la cabeza del paciente en posición neutra o semi‑Fowler
interventions.rationale: Facilita el paso del aire y reduce riesgo de aspiración

interventions.action: Evaluar capacidad de deglución antes de ofrecer alimentos o líquidos
interventions.rationale: Prevenir ingreso de contenido a vías respiratorias

interventions.action: Aspirar secreciones orofaríngeas según necesidad
interventions.rationale: Eliminar material que pueda ser aspirado

interventions.action: Evitar alimentos sólidos y líquidos calientes hasta que el edema disminuya
interventions.rationale: Reducir riesgo de obstrucción y aspiración

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre postura adecuada al comer y beber despacio
Observar tos, cambios en auscultación pulmonar y aumento de sibilancias

en.summary: Sudden swelling of deep skin and mucous membranes, often affecting the face, lips, tongue, and airways, frequently associated with hives.
key_points: Deep skin and mucous membrane swelling that can compromise the airway
May be accompanied by itchy hives
Common triggers: NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, foods, infections
Emergency if breathing difficulty or airway compromise
Treatment: antihistamines, corticosteroids, and epinephrine if airway involvement
Monitoring vital signs and oxygen saturation is essential

pathophysiology: Release of histamine and bradykinin from an allergic reaction
Increased capillary permeability in deep dermis and submucosa
Fluid extravasation into interstitial tissue producing edema
risk_factors: Use of NSAIDs or ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril)
signs_symptoms: Non‑itchy swelling of lips, eyelids, tongue, or face
Burning or pressure sensation in affected area
diagnostics: Medical history and focused airway exam
O₂ saturation and respiratory rate assessment
Allergy testing (IgE) if specific trigger suspected
C1‑esterase levels if hereditary angioedema considered
Complete blood count to rule out infection
treatment: Epinephrine IM 0.3 mg if respiratory compromise
Supplemental oxygen and airway support if needed
complications: Persistent edema >72 h with possible skin damage
nursing_care: Assess and document edema size every 15 min initially
Monitor O₂ saturation and respiratory rate
Maintain semi‑Fowler position to facilitate breathing
Administer medications per order and observe response
Prepare resuscitation equipment and epinephrine in case of deterioration
patient_teaching: Carry an epinephrine auto‑injector if prescribed by the physician
Seek immediate care if facial swelling or breathing difficulty occurs
Take antihistamines as directed and do not discontinue without consulting
Inform all healthcare professionals about your allergy

related_to: use of diuretics or ACE inhibitors
outcomes: Hydration: adequate level (stable weight, normal skin turgor)

interventions.action: Monitor fluid intake and output each shift
Assess skin and mucous membrane turgor frequently
Encourage clear fluid intake if no contraindication
Record changes in edema size
interventions.rationale: Observe trend of fluid loss or accumulation

interventions.action: Notify physician if signs of hypotension or tachycardia
Administer saline solution per order if replacement indicated

outcomes: Airway safety: no signs of aspiration during hospitalization
Respiratory function: O₂ saturation ≥95 % at rest

interventions.action: Maintain patient head in neutral or semi‑Fowler position
interventions.rationale: Facilitates airflow and reduces aspiration risk

interventions.action: Assess swallowing ability before offering food or liquids
interventions.rationale: Prevent entry of contents into airways

interventions.action: Aspirate oropharyngeal secretions as needed
interventions.rationale: Remove material that could be aspirated

interventions.action: Avoid solid foods and hot liquids until edema subsides
Educate patient on proper posture when eating and drinking slowly
Observe cough, changes in lung auscultation, and increased wheezing

summary.0.quote: This disorder involves swelling of the deeper skin layers and most commonly occurs in the face (eyelids, lips, tongue, cheeks), hands, feet, genitalia or throat.

key_points.0.quote: In rare cases, hives can cause a dangerous swelling in your airways, making it hard to breathe - which is a medical emergency.

key_points.1.quote: Hives are red and sometimes itchy bumps on your skin.

key_points.2.quote: This reaction is usually the result of exposure to triggers like food, medications, insect stings, physical stimuli, latex , blood transfusions, bacterial or viral infections, pet dander, plants, and pollen.

key_points.3.quote: In rare cases, hives can cause a dangerous swelling in your airways, making it hard to breathe - which is a medical emergency.

key_points.4.quote: Management of angioedema may include the use of epinephrine, antihistamines, or corticosteroids.

key_points.5.quote: The nursing assessment for urticaria should include vital signs as well as a review of the relevant body systems to identify potential causes and determine the case’s severity.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Angioedema is either histamine-mediated or bradykinin -mediated.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: Vascular permeability is increased and results in edema.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Table 19.4 is a drug prototype table for ACE inhibitors featuring lisinopril.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: This reaction is usually the result of exposure to triggers like food, medications, insect stings, physical stimuli, latex , blood transfusions, bacterial or viral infections, pet dander, plants, and pollen.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: People who have other allergies are more likely to get hives than other people.

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: Nonimmune-mediated reactions may be caused by medications and by physical or emotional stimuli that activate mast cells (Benedetti, 2021).

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Hives are red and sometimes itchy bumps on your skin.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: The patient should also be able to demonstrate how to properly administer their medications and be able to describe signs and symptoms like anaphylaxis, angioedema, difficulty swallowing, wheezing, difficulty breathing, peripheral tingling, and urticaria that is not resolving.

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Low levels of C4 proteins may indicate hereditary angioedema or acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency (Frank, 2024).

sections.treatment.1.quote: Corticosteroids inhibit histamine release by stabilizing mast cell membranes and reduce inflammatory effects of histamine.

sections.complications.0.quote: Airway management is the top priority with angioedema as airway obstruction can lead to hypoxia, brain damage, and death.

sections.complications.1.quote: Report side effects such as cough, angioedema, or anaphylactic reactions to their health care provider.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Interventions may be aimed at improving symptoms, administering medications, patient education about avoidance therapy, and promoting home-based care.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Medical therapies include avoiding the use of NSAIDs, limiting the use of items that can further aggravate the reaction, and eliminating the known or suspected allergen that caused the reaction.
